identity.title: Position: Political Neutrality in AI Is Impossible — But Here Is How to Approximate It

problem.claim: AI systems can exhibit political bias that influences users’ opinions and decisions.

gap.claim: The paper argues that treating complete political neutrality as a universally feasible fairness and safety solution overlooks its subjective nature and biases from training data, algorithms, and user interactions.

contributions.claim: Reframes political neutrality as an approximation rather than an attainable absolute, grounded in neutrality as a matter of degree.
Proposes eight neutrality-approximation techniques across three levels of conceptualizing AI, including trade-offs and implementation strategies.
Presents two concrete applications and assesses the framework at the output level of current large language models.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors distinguish approximation-based political neutrality from absolute neutrality and organize eight techniques across three AI-conceptualization levels.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report two concrete applications intended to illustrate the practicality of their proposed approximations.
The authors report an output-level assessment of the framework on current large language models as a demonstration of how it can be evaluated.

narrative_sequence.summary: Political bias in AI can influence user opinions and decisions.
Complete political neutrality is presented as infeasible and not universally desirable because neutrality is subjective and AI systems inherit multiple sources of bias.
The paper retains neutrality as an important goal while treating it as gradual and approximable rather than absolute.
It proposes eight techniques across three AI levels, illustrates them with two applications, and demonstrates output-level evaluation on current LLMs.

source_observation.claim: The paper explicitly replaces an unattainable absolute with practical proxies and pairs the proposal with stated trade-offs, implementation strategies, applications, and an evaluation demonstration.

lessons.interpretation: A difficult normative objective can become more actionable when operationalized as graded proxies whose costs and evaluation route are made explicit.
lessons.application: For a contested AI property, define an approximation target, enumerate measurable proxies, state their trade-offs, and show both a concrete use case and an evaluation procedure.
lessons.exception: This move is unsuitable when the task requires a strict binary guarantee or when proxy definitions would obscure rather than clarify the governing norm.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the eight techniques, three levels, two applications, trade-offs, implementation details, evaluation measures, or assessment outcomes.
The abstract does not establish whether the proposed approximations improve fairness, safety, or resistance to manipulation.
